tagline: See what you're not seeing — on one page.
problem: Each specialist answers its own question well, but a CISO doesn't want twenty answers — they want one picture and one next move. Without a view that brings them together, the most dangerous risk survives: the unknown unknowns nobody thought to ask a single tool about.
does: Ensemble Report reads what the whole pack found on its last release and puts it on one page, Ensemble Report: how exposed the estate is, where risk concentrates, what is converging, what is on the clock, the blind spots, and the next moves — including a recommended play and how much exposure it would remove. Every number opens the exact assets behind it.

glance.caption: Ensemble Report's At a glance after a release: how exposed (estate score, KEV, crown jewels, blind), where it concentrates, converging signals, on the clock, blind spots, pack coverage and next moves — each card opens its evidence in Explorer › Assets or the owning specialist, already filtered.

capabilities: every card opens its evidence: the exact assets (KEV, score ≥ 60, crown jewels, with KEV or blind, EOL, quantum-vulnerable …) or the owning specialist, already filtered.
all assets → seen by a specialist → credentialed → classified → owned → business-tiered, each step linked to the specialist that owns the gap.
assets no specialist saw, blind hosts, unclassified, unowned, no business tier, shadow AI.
the worst assets by fused score, with each specialist's points on each host; the estate as one square per asset.
signal stacks, the overlap map and cross-specialist surprises — where several specialists fire on the same assets.
patch KEV / critical, replace EOL, renew certificates, segment exposure or assign owners — with the exposure it would remove and the signals it neutralizes.
the digest of what moved since the last release.
how: Ensemble Report reads the cached results of the last Run the Ensemble plus Exposure Score's fused scores; it writes nothing. Evidence lists are computed on demand by the specialist that owns each number, so they match the card.
who: CISOs who want the estate on one page, VM leads running the morning stand-up, and anyone building executive reporting that survives questions.
better: Ensemble Report is where the Ensemble converges — Exposure Score's scores, Laelaps, Scan Health, Linnaeus, Ownership, Criticality Calibration, Pythia, Charon, Heimdall and the rest. Explorer › Assets shows the evidence behind each card, and Notify & Reports can send the briefing.
cta: Open Ensemble Report tomorrow morning — and see what you weren't seeing.
